27.0.0.en: The altar is made of acacia wood, which signifies the wood of the Cross, and it is in the shape of a rectangular solid, that is, the shape of a tomb, as a symbol of the death of Christ, for on this altar were offered the sacrifices that signify the crucified Christ who died for us (fig. 13). The dimensions of the altar are five cubits in length and five cubits in width, as a symbol of the five senses of man, which are sanctified by Christ the Redeemer in their spiritual striving, and as a symbol of the five offerings mentioned in the Book of Leviticus, which point to the crucified Christ. Its height is three cubits, as a symbol of the risen Christ, for He died for us and then rose on the third day. And because the altar is high, they would mostly go up to it by an inclined surface, since God forbade them to go up to the altars by steps (ch. 20:25). Figure (13:) The altar of burnt offering (the bronze altar)

27.1.0.en: Four horns are made for the altar at its four corners, and these horns are made from one block of wood with the corner post, not a horn fixed to the post by mortising. The horn signifies strength, because the redemption of Christ is strong and takes away all the sins of the world. The sacrifices were bound to the horns of the altar until they were slaughtered. And the wronged person would hold fast to the horns of the altar, proclaiming his clinging to God to save him from injustice and death.

27.1.1.en: The altar is overlaid with bronze plates, and bronze signifies endurance and steadfastness, as Christ endured sufferings for us on the Cross.

27.2.0.en: The requisites and instruments of the altar are all made of bronze, and they are:-

27.2.1.en: 1- Its pans: vessels in which the ashes of the burnt offerings are gathered to be cast outside the camp; the word is the plural of "pot," which may be used for cooking meat.

27.2.2.en: 2- Its shovels: the plural of "shovel," a scoop (spade) for gathering the ashes from the altar.

27.2.3.en: 3- Basins: the plural of "basin," a flat vessel like a washbowl, for gathering the blood of the slaughtered animals.

27.2.4.en: 4- Fleshhooks: the plural of "fleshhook," a three-pronged fork with a long handle for lifting pieces of meat from the altar or those placed in the pots.

27.2.5.en: 5- Firepans: the plural of "firepan," in which burning coals are placed; they may have been used to keep the holy fire while the ashes of the burnt offerings were removed or when the tent was moved from place to place (Lev 9:24).

27.3.0.en: A network grating surrounds the altar in its lower half, that is, to a height of a cubit and a half from the ground, so that the priests' feet cannot touch the altar when they approach to offer the sacrifices on it, out of respect for it, but touch only this network barrier made of bronze. At the top of this network barrier four rings are made at the corners of the altar, and these rings are made of bronze and fixed at its four corners, to put the two staves in them to carry the altar when moving camp.

27.4.0.en: A compass is made for the altar, surrounding it a little below its upper surface. It is most probably like a ledge around the altar, projecting 10-20 cm on all sides, so that if a piece of meat falls it falls on it and not on the ground.

27.5.0.en: He makes two staves of acacia wood and overlays them with bronze, which signifies the crucified Christ who endured sufferings for us.

27.6.0.en: The two staves are put into the bronze rings that are on the two sides of the altar.

27.7.0.en: The bronze altar consists of four walls and an upper top on which are the four horns, but it is hollow inside because it signifies the tomb. It is confirmed here that Moses saw all the details of the tent of meeting on the mountain in the form of pictures or models.

27.7.1.en: Endure sufferings for the sake of Christ, who endured sufferings for you and who is signified by this bronze altar, and do not murmur or compare yourself with others, but ask for God's help, and you will experience His fellowship, your will will be strengthened, and you will enjoy peace.

27.8.s.en: (2) The walls of the tent of meeting

27.8.0.en: The court of the tabernacle: that is, the outer court surrounding the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, in which are the laver and the bronze altar.

27.8.1.en: It tells us about the outer wall of the tent of meeting, inside which is a courtyard with the tabernacle in its midst. The bronze altar is in the courtyard at the entrance of the tent, then the laver, and after that the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies (figs. 14, 15). The south wall, that is, the one on the side toward the south, is 100 cubits long and is made of linen hangings. Southward: that is, the south, which is the left of one entering by the east door of the tent.

27.8.2.en: 100 cubits. The pillar of cloud and fire. North. 50 cubits. The laver. The altar of burnt offering. The tent of meeting. The outer court. Figure (14) The outer walls of the court of the tabernacle. (1) A pillar of bronze. (3) A hook of silver. (2) A curtain. (4) A rod of silver. (5) Pins. (6) A base of bronze. 15 cubits. 20 cubits. 15 cubits. A hanging of blue, purple, scarlet and linen. The outer gate or the east wall. Figure (15)

27.9.0.en: The south wall is hung on 20 pillars made of bronze, and the hooks, that is, their upper rings on which the hangings are hung, are made of silver. These bronze pillars are joined by crosswise pillars, which are rods, most probably fixed through the silver hooks, so that the whole wall is fixed as one unit. The pillars are fixed in the ground and are then also secured by pins on the inside and outside, drawn by cords from the top of the pillar, to protect the wall from the wind. The bronze pillars are fixed in bronze bases in the ground, and there may also be pins for the tabernacle, to which cords are tied to secure it on its three sides, the north, the west and the south.

27.10.0.en: The north wall is exactly like the south wall, standing on 20 pillars joined by silver rods, with the linen hangings hung on the bronze pillars, and it is likewise fixed in the ground with bronze pins tied with cords on the inside and outside.

27.11.0.en: The west wall is 50 cubits wide. Its linen hangings are fixed on ten bronze pillars fixed in the ground with bronze bases, and its silver rods are fixed in the silver hooks in the pillars to join the pillars together. It also has bronze pins tying it with cords on the inside and outside.

27.12.0.en: The east wall consists of two parts of the wall, each 15 cubits, fixed on three bronze pillars in the same form as the rest of the wall and with the same hangings, so that there are two sides, right and left, on the east, each 15 cubits, and between them the main gate of the tent of meeting, 20 cubits wide, before which is the bronze altar, then the laver, and after that the tabernacle itself.

27.13.0.en: The east gate is a curtain of linen embroidered with blue, purple and scarlet, hung on four pillars like the previous pillars but without pins. Entry was by lifting the curtain and entering from under it or beside it. It is noted that the curtain of the gate is different from the hangings of the wall, for it is embroidered in the colors blue, purple and scarlet, because Christ is the door, and He is the King of kings (purple), the Redeemer (scarlet) and the Dweller in heaven (blue) (fig. 15).

27.14.0.en: All the pillars of the wall are of bronze, and their bases fixed in the ground are also of bronze, while the rods that join them are of silver and are fixed in hooks of silver. The meaning of this is that Christ is the wall of our salvation, who endured all sufferings for us, that is, the bronze, and He is the word of God, that is, the silver. Every spiritual person ought to be firm in the word of God and endure sufferings for His sake (fig. 15).

27.15.0.en: The dimensions of the wall are 100 cubits in length and 50 cubits in width, while the height is five cubits. It is understood from this that the linen pieces from which the wall is made are each 5 cubits x 5 cubits, and each piece is fixed on two pillars.

27.16.0.en: It is noted that the vessels of the bronze altar, which people see, and likewise the pillars of the wall and its bases, are of bronze, so that whoever sees them may learn patience and endurance in the spiritual life.

27.16.1.en: Take care to guard your life with walls, which are the word of God in the Holy Bible, the guidance of your father of confession, your attachment to the means of grace, and partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord. In this way Christ will be a wall around your life and will keep it.

28.0.s.en: (1) Consecrating the priests and making garments for them

28.0.0.en: The head of the family was its priest in the age of the patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Then Moses performed the priestly work, and after that God chose Aaron and his sons to be priests to Him and asked Moses to do this, and they signify Christ the Great High Priest. The whole tribe of Levi helped the priests, the tribe that God set apart for His service, although Levi himself had sinned by killing the tribe of Shechem (Gen 34:25-30), but the mercy of God granted his descendants to be servants. The priests and Levites offered the sacrifices and offerings in the house of the Lord and took care of all the rites of worship in it and of its cleanliness and of moving it from place to place as God guided them, in addition to teaching the people the commandments of God and His worship, and examining sinners such as lepers, and they would decide their cleanness when God healed them.

28.1.0.en: He asked Moses to make garments of a particular form for the priests, suited to the great service that they would perform before God, so that the garments they wear during the service would be worthy of the glory and splendor of God.

28.1.1.en: A person's appearance helps him toward the life he wants. Just as the priests' garments are fitting for being before God, so the clothes of the children of God should be fitting for them and show before people that they are children of God. So take care in your appearance, lest you cause anyone to stumble.

28.2.0.en: Moses gathers the skilled craftsmen to make these garments, which proclaim that Aaron and his sons are consecrated, that is, set apart and dedicated to the service of God.

28.3.0.en: Wise hearted: those skilled in the various crafts.

28.3.1.en: He mentions the details of the priest's garments, which are the "breastplate," which is placed on the ephod, which is the outer garment, and under it the robe, and then the broidered coat, in addition to the mitre and the girdle, all of which will be detailed in this chapter (fig. 16). The high priest wore these garments during his ordinary service every day, but on the Day of Atonement he humbled himself and wore only garments of linen in order to enter the Holy of Holies in them (Lev 16:4).

28.4.0.en: These garments are made from materials that Moses collects from the people, and these materials have already been referred to and their meanings explained, and they are "gold, blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen (linen)."

28.5.0.en: The ephod is the outer garment; it is short and reaches the knees. It is made of linen, which signifies purity, blue, which signifies the heavenly life, purple, which signifies kingship, scarlet, which signifies the blood of Christ, and gold, which signifies God. The priest ought to be characterized by all this.

28.6.0.en: The ephod is made of two pieces joined together at the shoulders, and between them is an opening for the head, wider at the front than at the back, and the ephod is tied with a girdle, that is, a belt. That is, the ephod has no sleeves, like a vest.

28.7.0.en: A girdle or belt is made from the same cloth as the ephod; it is a belt tied around the waist to gather the ephod and all the priestly garments, and its two ends hang down from the waist in front toward the feet. This girdle signifies readiness and earnestness in work and spiritual striving, as any worker braces himself and ties up his waist so that his loose garments do not hinder him.

28.8.0.en: According to their birth: in the order of their birth, that is, the eldest and then the one younger than he.

28.8.1.en: God commanded Moses to bring two onyx stones, a kind of precious stone, and to engrave on each stone six names of the tribes of the children of Israel according to age, as an engraver engraves a signet, and to make for each stone a setting of gold around it, and they are fixed on the shoulders of Aaron to proclaim his responsibility for all the people, since he bears them on his shoulders, prays for them and cares for them, just as Christ carried the wood of the Cross on His shoulder for us, and He is our Great High Priest. His entering the Holy of Holies is an entering of all the people, carried on his shoulders, into the presence of God.

28.8.2.en: May you feel your responsibility for those around you, so that you pray for them, take care to draw them to the Church, show them your love and solve their problems.

28.9.0.en: Two chains of gold, plaited, are made, hanging from the two gold settings surrounding the two onyx stones.

28.10.0.en: The breastplate is the most important part of the high priest's garments, because in it are the Urim and the Thummim (v. 30), which reveal God's commands to His people. Therefore this breastplate was called the breastplate of judgment, because it proclaims God's judgment to His people.

28.10.1.en: The breastplate is made of the same cloth and materials as the ephod, which are gold, blue, purple, scarlet and fine twined linen (linen), and their meanings have been mentioned before (fig. 17).

28.11.1.en: It is made from a piece of cloth two spans long and a span wide, which is then folded, so that its length becomes a span and its width a span, and it is like a bag of cloth with its opening at the top.

28.12.0.en: Twelve precious stones are set on the breastplate in four rows, each containing three stones, and each stone is surrounded by a gold setting by which it is fixed on the breastplate. These precious stones are:

28.12.3.en: 3- Emerald: a stone of a dark red color which, in the rays of the sun, appears like a flame of fire.

28.12.4.en: 4- Ruby: its color is yellow inclining to red.

28.12.6.en: 6- White carnelian: a precious kind of carnelian.

28.12.7.en: 7- Cat's eye: a transparent stone with black spots, so it resembles the eye of a cat.

28.12.8.en: 8- Jade: a transparent stone with wavy lines.

28.12.9.en: 9- Amethyst: its color is purple, that is, red inclining to violet.

28.12.10.en: 10- Beryl: a transparent or green stone.

28.12.11.en: 11- Onyx: a stone with parallel lines.

28.12.12.en: 12- Jasper: a kind of precious crystal.

28.13.0.en: The name of a tribe is written on each stone, and by this God proclaims that Aaron enters before God with all the tribes, for Aaron is responsible for caring for them and prays for them. Aaron enters with the blood of animals and with the twelve tribes on his breast, and in this he signifies Christ, who offers His blood as redemption for all who believe in Him. Two things appear here:

28.13.1.en: 1- The high priest bears the names of the tribes of the children of Israel on his breast, that is, beside his heart, so he feels all their problems and needs, which he carries on his shoulders through the two stones on which their names are engraved.

28.13.2.en: 2- He feels for each individual of his people, for every tribe, indeed every individual, is a jewel in the eyes of the shepherd.

28.14.0.en: Two rings are made at the two ends of the breastplate at its top and sewn to it, and these two rings are tied by two braids of gold to the two settings in which the onyx stones are fixed, each inscribed with 6 names of the tribes and placed on Aaron's shoulder. Thus the breastplate is hung and suspended from above, that is, on the priest's breast, and tied to his shoulder, and around the breastplate on its four sides are twisted gold chains, so that they are like a cordon for it.

28.15.0.en: Two rings of gold are made and sewn to the lower end of the breastplate, and opposite them two other rings of gold are fixed in the ephod itself above the girdle, and the two lower rings of the breastplate are tied to the two rings above the girdle with a blue thread. Thus the breastplate is fixed at the top by the two gold chains and at the bottom by cloth threads of a blue color.

28.16.0.en: The breastplate is fixed on the ephod and bears the names of the twelve tribes, that is, when he enters the Holy Place or the Holy of Holies all the tribes enter with him. It is called the breastplate of judgment because by it God's judgment in the various affairs of the people is known. There are many opinions about how God's mind was proclaimed, among them that one or all of the stones inscribed with the names of the children of Israel fixed on the breastplate would light up (fig. 17). Figure (17:) The breastplate

28.17.2.en: The Urim and the Thummim are two stones placed inside the bag of the breastplate, and they are used to know God's judgment in the affairs of the people when the high priest enters the Holy Place for God to declare His will, and this is by means of:

28.17.3.en: 1- These stones lighting up or not lighting up.

28.17.4.en: 2- There is an opinion that on one of them was written "yes" and on the other "no," and God lights up one of them, and so the will of God is known.

28.17.5.en: May you ask God in all your needs to know His will, so that you submit to Him and not to your personal desires, and He will answer you and declare His mind if you are submissive to Him.

28.18.0.en: The robe is the garment worn under the ephod; it is longer than it and reaches below the knee, near the feet, and it is made of cloth of a blue color, that is, blue.

28.19.0.en: The robe is made in one piece, with the opening at its top for the head to go through, and a binding, that is, a band of cloth, is sewn on this opening to strengthen it so that it does not tear when the robe is put on or taken off, as coats of mail are strengthened, which are strong garments that warriors wear to protect them from arrows.

28.20.0.en: Small balls like a pomegranate are made of cloth or threads, some of them blue, some purple and others scarlet. Small bells are made, and a ball is hung, then a bell, that is, a little bell, and after that a ball and after it a bell, and so on, so that when the high priest enters the Holy of Holies the priests who are in the Holy Place do not see him but hear the sound of the bells. If he died inside the Holy of Holies, they would not hear the sound of the bells, and then they would draw him out by the rope tied to his foot into the Holy Place, because it is forbidden for anyone to enter the Holy of Holies except the high priest. In addition, the bells alert him to be exact in the worship of God and His service and in carrying out His commandments, lest He be angry with him and he die.

28.20.1.en: The pomegranates signify the fruits of the spiritual life that the priest and the people live, in addition to the fact that the seeds of the pomegranate are surrounded by a sweet red juice that signifies the blood of Christ, which cleanses us and adorns us with virtues. As for the little bells, that is, the bells, they signify:

28.20.2.en: 1- The importance of the word of God, which the priest teaches to the people.

28.20.4.en: 3- The priest's attentiveness and exactness in his service.

28.20.5.en: May you be attentive when you stand to pray or when you read the Holy Bible, for you are in the presence of God, surrounded by His angels. As you feel the fear of Him, He opens your mind to understand His words and to enjoy His presence.

28.21.0.en: Engraving of a signet: that is, as is engraved on a signet.

28.21.1.en: He makes a plate of gold and engraves on it the words "Holiness to the Lord," to place it on the mitre of the high priest. It was called a crown in (ch. 29:6) because it is placed above the forehead of the high priest.

28.22.0.en: The gold plate is fixed on the mitre above the forehead with blue threads, that is, blue threads, to proclaim that the priest is consecrated to God, so he lives in purity and does nothing but the service of God. The blue threads proclaim that he is heavenly and lives the heavenly life.

28.23.0.en: The mitre with its gold plate proclaims the purity of the priest and his consecration to God, so when God sees his purity He forgives the people their shortcomings in their offerings and gifts to God. This is what is meant by "the iniquity of the holy things," for the priest completes the deficiencies of his people's worship by his prayers on their behalf.

28.23.1.en: May you care for those around you who are far from God, so that you pray for them, fast, prostrate yourself and ask God's help for them. As God sees your striving and your intercession for them, He will support you and them.

28.24.0.en: The garments of the priests, who are the sons of Aaron, consist of the following:

28.24.1.en: 1- A coat like the high priest's, as mentioned before.

28.24.2.en: 2- A bonnet, which is a head covering made of linen, resembling a fez or a large high cap, and it may have a veil, that is, a piece of cloth hanging down at the back attached to the bonnet, like the garments of the present-day priests.

28.24.3.en: 3- A girdle, which is a piece of embroidered linen cloth tied around the waist with its end hanging down in front. All the priests' garments are of linen, a symbol of the purity and splendor that befit being in the presence of the great and glorified God.

28.25.0.en: The details of the ordination of the priests are mentioned here, which will be mentioned in the next chapter: he clothes them in their garments, anoints them with oil and consecrates them, that is, gives them sacrifices to offer before God.

28.26.0.en: He makes undergarments for the priests, which he calls breeches, from the waist to above the knee, and they signify modesty and the fear of God when entering the tent of meeting for the service and the offering of sacrifices, because if they neglect to wear these garments they sin against God and die in their iniquity.

28.26.1.en: These garments were for the service in the tent of meeting, but outside it they would wear their own garments as they wished.

28.26.2.en: In the Church of the New Testament the priests wear adorned white garments when they enter the sanctuary, for the following reasons:

28.26.3.en: 1- They befit the greatness of God in His sanctuary, so they wear garments of splendor.

28.26.4.en: 2- They call them and their people to purity when drawing near to God.

28.26.5.en: 3- As a continuation of God's commands in the Old Testament concerning the priests' garments, because all stand before God.

28.26.6.en: 4- In eternity they wear white garments (Rev 4:4, 6:11, 7:9, 15).

28.26.7.en: Your fear of God appears in your modesty when appearing before Him, so do not be preoccupied with appearance and clothes so that others may see you in them, but be as befits His presence. And when your relationship with Him grows, you will be modest at all times because He sees you.

28.26.8.en: The consecration of the priests: this chapter shows the steps of the ordination of the priests, which are:

28.26.9.en: 1- Washing with water as a sign of purity of heart (v. 4).

28.26.10.en: 2- Putting on the priestly garments, proclaiming the beginning of the new service filled with glory and splendor (vv. 5-9).

28.26.11.en: 3- Anointing with holy oil as evidence of their consecration and their being set apart for the service of God (v. 7).

28.26.12.en: 4- Offering a sin offering to make atonement for their sins (vv. 10-14).

28.26.13.en: 5- Offering a burnt offering to be a sweet savour before the Lord (vv. 15-18).

28.26.14.en: 6- Offering the ram of consecration as a peace offering, and waving parts of the sacrifice with the vegetable offering for their installation and their beginning the priestly service (vv. 19-25).

28.26.15.en: 7- Eating of the sacrifice as a sign of their fellowship with God and a reward for their blessed work (vv. 26, 27).
